column1: A millennium ago, stepwells were fundamental to life in the driest parts of India.
column2: 一千年前，在印度最干旱的地区，阶梯井对当地人的生活至关重要。

column1: Richard Cox travelled to north-western India to document these spectacular monuments from a bygone era
column2: 理查德·考克斯前往印度西北部，记录这些昔日留下的壮观古迹。

column1: During the sixth and seventh centuries, the inhabitants of the modern-day states of Gujarat and Rajasthan in north-western India developed a method of gaining access to clean, fresh groundwater during the dry season for drinking, bathing, watering animals and irrigation.
column2: 公元6至7世纪，今印度西北部古吉拉特邦和拉贾斯坦邦一带的居民想出了一种办法，可以在旱季取得清洁的地下淡水，用来饮用、洗澡、给牲畜饮水和灌溉。

column1: However, the significance of this invention - the stepwell - goes beyond its utilitarian application.
column2: 不过，阶梯井这项发明的意义超出了它的实际用途。

column1: Unique to this region, stepwells are often architecturally complex and vary widely in size and shape.
column2: 阶梯井为这一地区所特有，建筑结构往往很复杂，大小和形状也各不相同。

column1: During their heyday, they were places of gathering, of leisure and relaxation and of worship for villagers of all but the lowest classes.
column2: 在阶梯井的鼎盛时期，这些井是除社会最底层以外各阶层村民聚会、休闲放松和礼拜的场所。

column1: Most stepwells are found dotted round the desert areas of Gujarat (where they are called vav) and Rajasthan (where they are called baori), while a few also survive in Delhi.
column2: 大多数阶梯井散布在古吉拉特邦和拉贾斯坦邦的沙漠地带，在前者称为vav，在后者称为baori；德里也留存着少数几口。

column1: Some were located in or near villages as public spaces for the community; others were positioned beside roads as resting places for travellers.
column2: 有些阶梯井位于村中或村旁，是当地居民的公共活动场所；另一些则设在路旁，供旅人歇脚。

column1: As their name suggests, stepwells comprise a series of stone steps descending from ground level to the water source (normally an underground aquifer) as it recedes following the rains.
column2: 顾名思义，阶梯井由一连串从地面向下延伸的石阶构成，一直通往水源（通常是地下含水层），水位在雨季过后会逐渐下降。
column3: As their name suggests|顾名思义

column1: When the water level was high, the user needed only to descend a few steps to reach it; when it was low, several levels would have to be negotiated.
column2: 水位高时，用水的人只需下几级台阶就能取到水；水位低时，则得向下走好几层。

column1: Some wells are vast, open craters with hundreds of steps paving each sloping side, often in tiers.
column2: 有些井是巨大的露天深坑，每一面斜坡上都铺着数百级台阶，台阶往往分层排列。

column1: Others are more elaborate, with long stepped passages leading to the water via several storeys.
column2: 另一些井的构造更为复杂，长长的阶梯通道穿过数层，通往水面。

column1: Built from stone and supported by pillars, they also included pavilions that sheltered visitors from the relentless heat.
column2: 这些井以石材砌成，由石柱支撑，还设有亭阁，供访客躲避持续的酷热。

column1: But perhaps the most impressive features are the intricate decorative sculptures that embellish many stepwells, showing activities from fighting and dancing to everyday acts such as women combing their hair or churning butter.
column2: 不过，最引人注目的或许是点缀着许多阶梯井的那些精巧而繁复的装饰雕刻，上面刻画的活动从战斗、舞蹈，到女子梳头、搅制黄油等日常生活场景，无所不包。

column1: Down the centuries, thousands of wells were constructed throughout north-western India, but the majority have now fallen into disuse; many are derelict and dry, as groundwater has been diverted for industrial use and the wells no longer reach the water table.
column2: 几个世纪以来，印度西北部各地修建了数千口井，但如今大多数已停用。许多井年久失修，已经干涸，因为地下水被引作工业用水，井底已经够不到地下水面。
column3: Down the centuries|几个世纪以来
column8: fallen into disuse|逐渐废弃不用

column1: Their condition hasn’t been helped by recent dry spells: southern Rajasthan suffered an eight-year drought between 1996 and 2004.
column2: 近年的一段段干旱也无助于改善这些井的状况。1996年至2004年间，拉贾斯坦邦南部经历了长达八年的旱灾。

column1: However, some important sites in Gujarat have recently undergone major restoration, and the state government announced in June last year that it plans to restore the stepwells throughout the state.
column2: 不过，古吉拉特邦一些重要遗址最近已得到大规模修复。去年6月，邦政府宣布计划修复全邦的阶梯井。

column1: In Patan, the state’s ancient capital, the stepwell of Rani Ki Vav (Queen’s Stepwell) is perhaps the finest current example.
column2: 在该邦的古都帕坦，拉尼·基·瓦夫阶梯井（王后阶梯井）或许是现存最出色的实例。

column1: It was built by Queen Udayamati during the late 11th century, but became silted up following a flood during the 13th century.
column2: 这座井由乌达亚玛蒂王后于11世纪末修建，后来因13世纪的一场洪水而淤塞。

column1: But the Archaeological Survey of India began restoring it in the 1960s, and today it is in pristine condition.
column2: 不过，印度考古局从20世纪60年代开始修复这座井，如今它已完好如初。
column3: Archaeological Survey of India|n. 印度考古局

column1: At 65 metres long, 20 metres wide and 27 metres deep, Rani Ki Vav features 500 sculptures carved into niches throughout the monument.
column2: 拉尼·基·瓦夫阶梯井长65米、宽20米、深27米，遍布井内的壁龛中刻有500尊雕像。

column1: Incredibly, in January 2001, this ancient structure survived an earthquake that measured 7.6 on the Richter scale.
column2: 令人难以置信的是，这座古建筑在2001年1月一场里氏7.6级的地震中幸存了下来。
column3: Incredibly|adv. 令人难以置信的是

column1: Another example is the Surya Kund in Modhera, northern Gujarat, next to the Sun Temple, built by King Bhima I in 1026 to honour the sun god Surya.
column2: 另一个例子是古吉拉特邦北部莫德赫拉的苏里亚昆德池，紧邻太阳神庙。这座神庙由比马一世于1026年为敬奉太阳神苏里亚而建。

column1: It actually resembles a tank (kund means reservoir or pond) rather than a well, but displays the hallmarks of stepwell architecture, including four sides of steps that descend to the bottom in a stunning geometrical formation.
column2: 它其实更像一座蓄水池（kund意为水库或池塘），而不像一口井，但它展现了阶梯井建筑的典型特征，例如四面的台阶一直向下延伸到池底，构成令人惊叹的几何图案。

column1: The terraces house 108 small, intricately carved shrines between the sets of steps.
column2: 各组台阶之间的平台上，有108座雕刻精细的小神龛。

column1: Rajasthan also has a wealth of wells.
column2: 拉贾斯坦邦也有大量这样的井。
column3: a wealth of|大量的；丰富的

column1: The ancient city of Bundi, 200 kilometres south of Jaipur, is renowned for its architecture, including its stepwells.
column2: 本迪古城位于斋浦尔以南200公里，以建筑闻名，其中就包括阶梯井。

column1: One of the larger examples is Raniji Ki Baori, which was built by the queen of the region, Nathavatji, in 1699.
column2: 较大的阶梯井中有一座叫拉尼吉阶梯井，由当地王后纳塔瓦特吉于1699年修建。

column1: At 46 metres deep, 20 metres wide and 40 metres long, the intricately carved monument is one of 21 baoris commissioned in the Bundi area by Nathavatji.
column2: 这座古迹深46米、宽20米、长40米，雕刻精细，是纳塔瓦特吉在本迪一带委托修建的21座阶梯井之一。

column1: In the old ruined town of Abhaneri, about 95 kilometres east of Jaipur, is Chand Baori, one of India’s oldest and deepest wells; aesthetically it’s perhaps one of the most dramatic.
column2: 斋浦尔以东约95公里处是阿巴内里古镇的遗址。昌德阶梯井坐落于此，是印度最古老、最深的井之一；论外观，它或许也是最壮观的井之一。

column1: Built in around 850 AD next to the temple of Harshat Mata, the baori comprises hundreds of zigzagging steps that run along three of its sides, steeply descending 11 storeys, resulting in a striking pattern when seen from afar.
column2: 这座阶梯井约建于公元850年，紧邻哈沙特·玛塔神庙。数百级台阶沿井的三面呈之字形排列，陡然向下延伸十一层，从远处看，形成一幅引人注目的图案。

column1: On the fourth side, verandas which are supported by ornate pillars overlook the steps.
column2: 在井的第四面，装饰华丽的柱子支撑着游廊，从廊上可以俯瞰台阶。

column1: Still in public use is Neemrana Ki Baori located just off the Jaipur-Delhi highway.
column2: 尼姆拉纳阶梯井就在斋浦尔至德里的公路旁，至今仍供公众使用。

column1: Constructed in around 1700, it is nine storeys deep, with the last two being underwater.
column2: 这口井约建于1700年，有九层深，最下面两层浸在水中。

column1: At ground level, there are 86 colonnaded openings from where the visitor descends 170 steps to the deepest water source.
column2: 在地面这一层，有86个带柱廊的入口。游客从这里往下走170级台阶，就能到达最深处的水源。
column3: At ground level|在地面这一层

column1: Today, following years of neglect, many of these monuments to medieval engineering have been saved by the Archaeological Survey of India, which has recognised the importance of preserving them as part of the country’s rich history.
column2: 这些见证中世纪工程技艺的古迹曾长期无人照管。如今，印度考古局已抢救了其中许多座。该局已认识到，这些古迹是印度丰富历史的一部分，保护它们十分重要。
column12: as part of|作为……的一部分

column1: Tourists flock to wells in far-flung corners of north-western India to gaze in wonder at these architectural marvels from hundreds of years ago, which serve as a reminder of both the ingenuity and artistry of ancient civilisations and of the value of water to human existence.
column2: 游客纷纷涌向印度西北部偏远地区的古井，惊叹于这些建于数百年前的建筑奇观。它们既让人想起古代文明的创造力与艺术才华，也提醒人们水对人类生存的重要性。
column5: gaze in wonder at|惊叹地凝望
column7: serve as a reminder of|使人想起；提醒人们
